solutionSql: SELECT s.customer_id, COUNT(*)::integer AS shipments, ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg))::integer AS avg_kg FROM shipments AS s WHERE s.customer_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6 GROUP BY s.customer_id ORDER BY s.customer_id;

rules.howSolved: COUNT(*) counts every shipment row, including those with a NULL weight.
ROUND is applied to the numeric AVG, then cast to integer.
AVG skips NULL weights, while COUNT(*) in the same query does not.

ambiguities: 'rounded to the nearest whole kilogram' does not say how an exact .5 is rounded. PostgreSQL ROUND on numeric rounds half away from zero, which is what I used.

'For customers with ids 1 through 6' does not say whether a customer in that range with no shipments is listed. I grouped over shipments, so one with no shipments is not listed. All six customers have shipments in the sample, nulls and ties datasets.
notes: Read-only item. Ran without error on sample, nulls and ties. The uncertainty is the same as c6-i4: the half-kilogram tie rule and the customer-listing wording. Solve time is an estimate.
